slot.brief: For XeF2/XeF4/XeF6, ask hybridisation and geometry (or number of lone pairs); e.g. shape of XeF4 with bond angles.

stem: According to VSEPR, how many lone pairs are on Xe and what is the molecular shape of $\text{XeF}_6$?

verdicts.working: Xe has 8 valence electrons; after forming six Xe–F bonds, one lone pair remains. VSEPR predicts a distorted octahedral shape.

working:
Xe has $8$ valence electrons; six Xe–F bonds leave one lone pair on Xe.\n$\text{XeF}_6$ is $\text{AX}_6\text{E}$ and has a distorted octahedral shape.

Independent check: Xe has 8 valence electrons; after forming six Xe–F bonds, one lone pair remains. VSEPR predicts a distorted octahedral shape.
solution:
Xe has $8$ valence electrons; forming six Xe–F bonds leaves one lone pair on Xe.
Thus, $\text{XeF}_6$ is $\text{AX}_6\text{E}$ and has a distorted octahedral shape.
